messages:
sara: Quick heads-up — after the driver update to 535.86 on staging, H100 thin-batch (bs=1) seq=2048 token-gen shows ~6% lower throughput vs 530.41. Can someone triage? I have bench logs.

devon: Can you paste the exact command + env? also which model and quantization?

sara: Repro command:
```
python bench_tokens.py --model redwood/rlhf-7b --gpu H100 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --driver 535.86 --quant none --runs 20
```
Logs (summary):
```
530.41: avg 48.9 tok/s, p50 20ms, p99 120ms
535.86: avg 45.9 tok/s, p50 22ms, p99 140ms
```

matt: I ran same bench on L40S (driver 535.86) and didn't see regression — L40S avg 46.1 tok/s (baseline ~46.0). Could be H100-specific kernel/regression.

kevin: I spun up H100 dev box, ran both drivers. Confirming older driver (530.41) is faster. Quick diff in nvprof shows extra memcpy stalls in attention kernels on 535.86.

ci-bot: perf-bench/staging/h100-thin-batch failed: https://ci.internal/reports/1789456123 — p95 increased by 14% — full logs uploaded.

perf-bot: Flamegraphs uploaded: https://perf.internal/flame/1789456123 — attention_matmul shows 8% more self-time on 535.86 vs 530.

devon: Assigning self to triage. Plan: reproduce with smaller seq and attach cuobjdump + kernel timings, compare cuBLAS/cuDNN versions. If reproduces, open infra-ticket to vendor with kernel traces.

sara: Thanks — ping me when you need VMs or extra runs. Also tagging @eng-infra for driver rollout hold.

kevin: Quick note — when I forced compute cap to 350W the regression shrank. Might be power management fallback on new driver.

matt: Good data point. Adding to the ticket: power policy + MIG state check.

devon: created perf ticket INF-5423 and linked logs/flamegraphs. Anyone with spare H100 can add more run artifacts there. ETA first pass by EOD tomorrow. :+1:

sara: Great. Leaving the staging rollout on hold until we have a root cause. Thanks all. :ok_hand:
